evidence_spans: These families in hardware speed up the workloads by 12.6% on average and by up to 80.2%.
From the discovered families, we simulate 30 of them in a cycle-accurate architectural simulator and implement them in RTL.
We measure the end-to-end application performance with Scarab [55, 68], configured after an Emerald Rapids core (Table 2).
The simulations show that these units speed up the workloads by 12.6% on average and by up to 80.2%, while the area of an average unit is only 0.37% of a core.
CLM-ARCH-0244.statement: The 30 hardware specialization families achieve up to an 80.2% speedup across the evaluated workloads.
